answers.text: Fixed format: drop-off time, pallet count, damage noted, in that order, three lines only. If there's no damage mentioned, I'd still put a line saying 'none noted' rather than leave it out.
Time, customer, topic, outcome per entry, then a count of how many need a follow-up call.
The 23rd doesn't work — 8am plus six hours finishes early afternoon the same day, not the next one. That's the bit I'd flag before it's filed.
96 to 118 is closer to a 23% increase than the 20% stated, so that needs fixing.
Output 2, since the 940 and 827 are right there to check. Output 1 is just the final number.
Email 2, it has the actual volume figures. Email 1 doesn't say where the expectation of a better rate comes from — though if that were backed up, it could probably go out too.
1. No, home address stays out. 2. Yes. 3. No, that budget's not signed off. 4. I'd hold that back as well. 5. No.
I'd hold back the rates and be careful with the NDA clause. Not sure about the rest, would check first.
I'd have a step where some of the reconciled figures get checked against the warehouse system before it's sent out.
The extraction step is the one to watch, and the gate really needs to be before the payment note goes out automatically.
